client_profile:
Bharat Manufacturing Industries Limited and its subsidiaries Bharat Steel Limited and Bharat Logistics LLP hold personal data across the employee lifecycle, including workers engaged in steel plants and industrial equipment operations, contractor and vendor contacts, dealer and customer personnel, and transport and fleet-related identifiers managed by the logistics arm. Data is typically generated through HR and payroll systems, shift and safety records, CCTV and plant access controls, e-commerce and dealer portals, logistics consignment booking, grievance helplines, and marketing or stakeholder outreach, alongside routine IT and CCTV telemetry.

An impact assessment would map each dataset to lawful grounds under the DPDP Act, 2023, with employee data largely processed under contractual necessity rather than consent, and consents elsewhere meeting the Act's notice, granularity and withdrawal standards. The assessment would evaluate purpose limitation, retention schedules, data minimisation, breach notification readiness, Notice Manager and Data Principal request mechanisms, Significant Data Fiduciary obligations, processor agreements, cross-border transfer implications, and grievance redressal timelines across all three entities.

categories.title: Employee & Workforce Data
categories.summary: Steel plants and equipment units employ large factory and office workforces, generating HR, payroll, attendance and statutory contribution records.
bullets: Name, employee ID, address, family and nominee details
Salary, bank account, PF, ESI and TDS records
Biometric or card-based attendance and shift data
Recruitment, appraisal, disciplinary and exit records
Contractor and migrant-worker deployment records
Statutory registers under Labour and wages laws

categories.title: Occupational Health & Safety Data
categories.summary: Hazardous steel-making operations require occupational health surveillance, injury tracking and safety compliance records for workers and contractors.
bullets: Medical fitness and periodic health examination records
Accident, injury and occupational disease reports
Gas exposure, noise and heat-stress monitoring records
Emergency drill and evacuation participant data
Safety training and certification records

categories.title: Customer & Dealer Data
categories.summary: Industrial equipment and steel sales involve B2B customers, dealers and channel partners whose contacts and transaction records are processed.
bullets: Contact persons, designations and business communication details
Quotations, purchase orders and contract documentation
Gstin, invoicing and payment history linked to individuals
Dealer and distributor onboarding and KYC records
Warranty, complaint and service-call histories

categories.title: Supplier & Vendor Data
categories.summary: Procurement of raw materials, consumables and services processes data of supplier proprietors, contacts and deployed site personnel.
bullets: Proprietor, partner and authorised signatory details
Vendor onboarding, PAN, GST and banking details
Purchase orders, quotations and correspondence
Vendor personnel deployed at plants for services
Audit, quality and performance assessment records

categories.title: Transport & Logistics Data
categories.summary: Bharat Logistics LLP moves steel and equipment by road, processing driver, fleet and consignment-contact personal data.
bullets: Driver licences, identity proof and contact numbers
Trip, GPS, e-way bill and consignment records
Transporter and fleet-owner operator details
Delivery proof, signature and POD photographs
Incident, claims and insurance documentation

categories.title: Visitor & Premises Security Data
categories.summary: Restricted industrial plants log visitor identities and CCTV footage for security and safety across group entities.
bullets: Visitor name, photo ID, vehicle number and host details
Gate entry-exit logs and digital visitor registers
CCTV and video surveillance footage at plant perimeters
Contractor and temporary pass-holder data
Incident logs involving visitors

categories.title: Website & Digital Channel Data
categories.summary: The corporate website and enquiry portals capture personal data from prospective buyers, Careers applicants and other website users.
bullets: Contact forms, enquiry and callback requests
Job application and careers portal submissions
Newsletter, feedback and survey responses
IP address, cookies and website analytics data
Email and phone correspondence with enquiries

categories.title: Statutory & Regulatory Data
categories.summary: Steel manufacturing and logistics attract environmental, tax, factory and law-enforcement disclosures of identifiable individuals.
bullets: Factory and inspectorate returns naming responsible persons
GST, customs and tax filings with signatory details
Environmental consent and pollution-board declarations
Government inspections, licenses and permits
Data shared with law enforcement under legal obligation

categories.title: Director & Key Managerial Personnel Data
categories.summary: Group entities Bharat Steel Limited and Bharat Logistics LLP process DIN, KYC and ownership data of directors and partners.
bullets: Director Identification Numbers and KYC documents
Signatory and authorisation records for bank accounts
LLP partner identity and profit-share details
Board meeting attendance and resolution records
Shareholding and beneficial ownership declarations

processing_bullets: Personal data, including employee identity, payroll and contact details, is collected directly from individuals and through HR, payroll and attendance systems operated by Bharat Manufacturing Industries Limited and its subsidiary entities.

Worker data comprising biodata, statutory identity records and next-of-kin details is collected from contractors and shop-floor employees of Bharat Steel Limited for employment administration and statutory compliance under applicable labour and factory laws.

Customer and contact person data is collected directly, from purchase orders and from publicly available business registers by Bharat Logistics LLP to enable freight booking, consignment tracking, invoicing and regulatory documentation.

Personal data is processed to operate and manage contracts, deliver industrial equipment and logistics services, administer vendor and customer relationships, discharge statutory obligations and pursue legitimate business interests of the group.

KYC documents, GST records, bank details and authorised signatory information are collected from business counterparties for customer due diligence, invoicing, payments, audit trails and anti-money-laundering compliance.

Personal data is shared with group entities, banks, insurers, statutory authorities, transporters, third-party service providers and professional advisers on a need-to-know basis under written contracts and lawful disclosures.

Sensitive personal data is stored on group servers, cloud platforms and physical records at manufacturing plants, depots and offices, with access restricted by role-based controls aligned with DPDP security safeguard obligations.

Retention periods are governed by statutory, contractual and audit requirements, including tax, factory, environmental and logistics records; data is securely erased or anonymised once the stated purpose and legal retention periods are met.

Employee data supports payroll, benefits, training, occupational health and safety monitoring, disciplinary administration and workforce planning across steel manufacturing and industrial equipment operations of the group entities.

Cross-location processing and transfers occur among group entities, plants, depots and service providers, involving disclosures to data fiduciaries and processors, including potential cross-border transfers, subject to DPDP consent and notice requirements.
